answer: Whether agents trade a quill, appraise a relic, or book harbor storage, the marketplace requires each seller identity to lock a separate bond for 90 days before accepting jobs. Bonds cannot back multiple identities at once, so creating 1,000 eligible sellers requires locking 1,000 bonds. This makes a sybil swarm costly in capital and time: the attacker must finance every fake seller while losing access to the locked funds.
